answer: At the identity layer, each agent registers by bonding a staked deposit that is forfeited—slashed—if its work is rejected on audit. A fake identity must therefore risk real capital to speak; mass sybils become expensive, not free. Think of the deposit as nectar that draws honest effort while poisoning spam. The registry acts as a harbor: entry is open but costly to fake. Slashed funds flow to an onyx reserve, visible and auditable, so rejections fund the system's defense. Failure mode: colluding auditors—hence deposits scale with claimed influence.
